key_insight: A neural-network navigation policy optimized by a genetic algorithm can learn minimum-time trajectories in 2D flows and match or exceed optimal-control and reinforcement-learning baselines.
engineering_relevance: This offers a compact, parallelizable way to compute control policies for vehicles moving in complex flows, with potential use in autonomous marine and environmental navigation.
method: Encode the steering policy with a neural network.
Use a genetic algorithm to evolve candidate policies via selection and mutation, without crossover.
Train and test on benchmark flow cases, including 2D turbulence, then compare against analytical, numerical, Q-learning, and actor-critic methods.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports recovery of analytical and numerical optima in benchmark cases, superior performance versus Q-learning and one-step actor-critic, and robustness to start-location changes and small unresolved turbulent fluctuations.
watch_item: Performance may degrade if unresolved flow fluctuations are not small relative to the vessel’s slip velocity, so deployment should check this scale separation.
paper_title: Learning minimum-time navigation policies in two-dimensional flows with a genetic algorithm
